story_type: icebreaker leads a fuel tanker through Antarctic sea ice
hook: Two years of fuel, one channel through Antarctic ice.
narration: This six hundred foot tanker had to reach Antarctica through a channel of broken sea ice.
It was the Stena Polaris, carrying fuel for McMurdo Station, the largest U.S. base on the continent.
The fuel was loaded in Greece before Christmas, and the tanker sailed all the way to the Ross Sea.
A few days earlier, the Coast Guard Cutter Polar Star had finished cutting a seven mile channel through fast ice.
Fast ice is sea ice frozen to the shore. An icebreaker rides up onto it, and its weight cracks it apart.
Then the cutter led the tanker in through the brash ice of that channel, and later led it back out.
Its cargo was meant to cover all of the station's fuel for two years.
outcome: The Stena Polaris made it through and arrived safely at the McMurdo ice pier on Jan. 20.
title: 600 foot tanker through Antarctic ice
description:
In January 2026 the Coast Guard Cutter Polar Star led the fuel tanker Stena Polaris through a channel of sea ice in the Ross Sea to McMurdo Station, Antarctica, during Operation Deep Freeze 2026.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Christopher Bokum, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/994313/uscgc-polar-star-wagb-10-escorts-motor-vessel-stena-polaris-through-ice-covered-ross-sea-mcmurdo-station-during
